payload.note: Delivery-Warrant preparation (part of the release/signing handoff). war next shows every delivery Warrant's own next step is 'war sign <alias>' - authorization - before any agent work is offered, so the signature gates the whole path rather than closing it. What was worth doing first was making the plans substantive: 12 of the 21 had zero machine-readable obligations, so 'obligations.valid' passed vacuously. KLM-WAR-0012 (7), 0013 (4), 0014 (6) and 0015 (5) now carry 22 obligations between them, each naming a bounded scope and evidence that exists - tests by name (v4_moves_sessions_to_legacy_and_clears_active, write_tools_play_move_reports_the_current_revision_on_conflict, evidence_fingerprint_changes_hash, approvals tests) or CDP scripts by their PASS marker (AI_APPROVALS_PASS, AI_CONTEXT_PASS, AI_CROSS_BOARD_PASS, AI_SESSION_PASS, AI_STREAM_PASS). Where something is not demonstrated the obligation says so: KLM-WAR-0012 OBL-007 (the 2 MB session size guard) reads as unestablished because no test drives the refusal. war admin compile rebuilt the generated views and war check --generated reports 153 pass, 0 error, no drift. Authorization requests are drafted for all four (contract digests 70d5673a03b9 / 2d962884e55f / fad8003fe927 / 21ca9976a756, eligible authorizer QuiteTall). war sign resolve --dry-run reports 10 of 13 requirements unmet - correct for a Warrant not yet authorized, delivered or verified. The other 17 Warrants have no obligations because their work is not implemented; writing them now would describe checks that cannot run. BLOCKED ON A PERSON: war sign <alias> for each.
